Subject: Dedicated sizing — expected peak token throughput + SLOs

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo. We’re trying to finalize internal sizing and want a conservative estimate for a Dedicated slab if we sign. A few specifics from our side: 
- Production traffic: bursty batch of inference jobs plus real-time chat. Peak observed on pilot: ~9k tokens/sec sustained over 10–15 minutes.
- Typical generation: median response 160 tokens, tail ~800 tokens.
- SLOs: 95th latency target for interactive chat <= 750ms (end-to-end). For batch jobs, throughput matters more than latency.

Can Redwood provide a model-by-model tokens/sec projection and recommended headroom for committed capacity (we’re considering both A100 and H100 nodes)? Also we need procurement timeline constraints (lead time for Dedicated) and a one-page ops checklist for our infra team.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our finance committee meets next Thursday.

Thanks,
Samira

On Mon, Nov 15, 2026 at 11:03 AM Aditya Rao wrote:
> Samira — thanks for the specifics. We can put together a short model-level forecast and a recommended commitment plan.

Hi all — attaching a compact capacity model (peregrine_capacity_model.xlsx) and a 1-page SLO mapping (peregrine_slo_matrix.pdf). Summary of our findings and recommended safe-commit slab below.

Quick assumptions used in the sheet:
- Production model candidates: open-70B-q4f16 (large), redwood-13B-int8 (mid), redwood-7B-int8 (small).
- Target workload mix (pilot -> projected prod): 55% interactive chat (latency-sensitive), 45% batch. Peak observed: 9k tokens/sec (you provided); we size to 1.5x peak headroom by default.
- Request profile: median 160 tokens / req; tail 800 tokens / req.

Measured tokens/sec per GPU (baseline configs) — these are practical end-to-end estimates including KV-cache behavior and average prompt length:
- H100 (4x HBM, optimized batch packing): open-70B-q4f16 -> ~420 tokens/sec per GPU; redwood-13B-int8 -> ~1,050 tokens/sec; redwood-7B-int8 -> ~2,200 tokens/sec.
- A100 (same batch/prompt): open-70B-q4f16 -> ~280 tokens/sec per GPU; redwood-13B-int8 -> ~720 tokens/sec; redwood-7B-int8 -> ~1,500 tokens/sec.

Sizing guidance (conservative):
- If you pick open-70B-q4f16 as primary and want 1.5x headroom on your 9k peak -> target capacity = 13.5k tokens/sec. On H100 that’s 13,500 / 420 ≈ 33 GPUs -> recommend 36-GPU slab (allow extra reserve for rolling updates). On A100 that’s ~48 GPUs -> recommend 52-GPU slab.
- For redwood-13B-int8 primary: 13,500 / 1,050 ≈ 13 GPUs -> recommend 16-GPU slab on H100 (24 GPUs on A100; recommend 28-GPU slab).
- For redwood-7B-int8 primary: 13,500 / 2,200 ≈ 7 GPUs -> recommend 8-GPU slab on H100 (10 GPUs on A100; recommend 12-GPU slab).

Latency fit notes (interactive chat 95th <= 750ms):
- open-70B on H100 with target slab above and continuous prefix KV caching should meet 95th for typical 160-token median responses (we observe ~420 t/s -> ~0.38s for 160 tokens amortized, plus network/aggregation -> fits under 750ms in our tests). Tail (800 tokens) will exceed the interactive SLO if generated synchronously; we recommend streaming/early-commit patterns or routing long generations to batch paths.

Operational callouts / risks:
- Warm-up/KV-cache: models see a significant token/sec uplift after warmed prefix; cold-starts will reduce effective tokens/sec — include pre-warming steps in the ops checklist.
- Quantization regression risk: open-70B-q4f16 yields large model-size savings but confirm quality on your eval set; we can run a short eval harness.
- Auto-burst: if you want short bursts above committed slab, we can propose a burst pool (3–5 GPUs) at market rates; this avoids oversizing the main slab.

Procurement and lead time (laura_bennett to confirm): typical Dedicated provisioning for a 36-GPU H100 slab is ~6–8 weeks from signed order (procurement, network setup, capacity allocation). We can compress for priority deals but would need a signed commitment + initial deposit.

Next steps proposed:
- Samira: share 24h telemetry + prompt samples.
- We’ll run a quick 48-hour internal simulation using your traffic to validate tokens/sec and tail latencies (deliverable: adjusted slab recommendation).
- Laura: send procurement timeline + contract milestones.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
